claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution; components inside a package inherit the package's version.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.

Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`, which sends package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from Pulumi.yaml can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit).

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary alongside per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy), and its version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
Pulumi recommends that a repository contain exactly one Pulumi package; multi-package repositories must release in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Pulumi does not recommend a single monorepo with one giant package for all components; releasing unrelated components in one package versions every component identically, violating semver.
The linked pages exist: Private Registry concept page, pulumi_package_publish CLI page, packaging-components anchors, and publishing-packages guide.
